Article Title: 'BJP like Angad's foot': Amit Shah warns Akhilesh, says SP won't return to power in UP for 30 years
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Friday sharpened his attack against the Samajwadi Party and said that it would remain out of power in Uttar Pradesh for the next 30 years.Addressing the Bharatiya Janata Party's state working committee meeting in Lucknow, Shah said that while the SP ordered firing on Ram devotees, the BJP built the Ram temple in Ayodhya."I want to ask them, on what grounds do they talk about forming a government? They ordered firing on Ram devotees, while we have built the Ram temple," he said, referring to the events of October 30, 1990, when police opened fire on kar sevaks in Ayodhya.“Akhilesh Babu, mark my words, your party will not form the government in Uttar Pradesh for the next 30 years. The people will not forgive even your third generation," he added.The home minister also said that the BJP in Uttar Pradesh could not be dislodged as the government had firmly established itself in the state."The BJP government in Uttar Pradesh is like Angad's foot. Nobody can move it. The BJP is going to form the government again. There should be no doubt about it," he said.Moreover, Shah also declared that if the BJP forms the government in Uttar Pradesh for a third time, the UCC will be implemented in the state."This time, when the government comes to power, UCC will be implemented in Uttar Pradesh. UCC has already been implemented in many states," he said.Shah also attacked opposition parties over their allegations of vote theft and compared their complaints to a team blaming the umpire after losing a match."After losing the match, they are blaming the umpire and alleging vote theft. The BJP is ready for a discussion in Parliament. Let them come today and convene a special session. We are ready to answer every question. Let there be a discussion in Parliament," he said.This comes as the BJP's state working committee meeting was held at the Dr Ram Manohar Lohia National Law University auditorium. The meeting was chaired by BJP state president and Union minister of state for finance Pankaj Chaudhary.Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath , deputy chief ministers Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak, BJP state in-charge Vinod Tawde and national general secretary Smriti Irani were among those present.
Article Summary: Union home minister Amit Shah sharpened his attack against the Samajwadi Party. He said that while the SP ordered firing on Ram devotees, the BJP built the Ram temple. Shah also declared that if the BJP forms the government in Uttar Pradesh for a third time, the UCC will be implemented in the state.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: A helicopter with six people onboard crashed near Joshimath in Uttarakhand’s Chamoli district while travelling from Badrinath to Dehradun. One pilot and five passengers were on board the chopper. The wreckage of a helicopter has been found.The helicopter, reportedly operated by Charlie X-ray Company, was reported missing near Hathi Parvat, prompting authorities to deploy two other choppers to locate it.Police, SDRF, Army and ITBP personnel have been dispatched to the site for relief and rescue operations, officials told PTI."At 14.21hrs, information was received from the SDM Joshimath regarding the crash landing of a helicopter above Chai village in the Joshimath area. In this regard, UCADA officials stated that the location of a Trans Bharat helicopter, which was flying from Badrinath to Sahastradhara, is showing near the Army Camp above Chai village," Sub-Inspector Manohar Kanyal, Joshimath Post told news agency ANI.Uttarakhand CM Pushkar Singh Dhami said the aircraft crashed near Chayee village, close to Joshimath, and that a joint rescue operation was underway involving the district administration, disaster management department and State Disaster Response Force (SDRF).“We have received the unfortunate news of a helicopter crash near Chayee village, close to Joshimath. A joint rescue operation is being conducted by the district administration, disaster management department, and SDRF,” Dhami wrote in a post on X.He added that he was personally monitoring the situation and that instructions had been issued to airlift the seriously injured to advanced medical facilities for treatment.

Article Title: It only takes one rumour: How a small trigger can lead to a deadly stampede
Article Text:
Stampede at Kolkata pandal during Durga Puja claimed 19 lives.

The anatomy of a stampede

Psychology of the crowd

How should police act and react?

Preparing for the unexpected

NEW DELHI: It begins with a rumour, feeds on panic and ends in tragedy. A stampede can turn a celebration into chaos within minutes, leaving thousands gathered in joy struggling to find a way out. In a tightly packed crowd, even a small disturbance can have deadly consequences.A similar script played out in Kolkata on October 17. On the night of Maha Saptami during Durga Puja, pandal-hoppers gathered in large numbers at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin pandal. The crowd swelled further after a sudden spell of rain prompted people waiting outside to seek shelter, while visitors near the exit stopped moving.An announcement over the public address system warning that the pandal was about to collapse added to the panic. Investigators believe several factors contributed to the stampede, including overcrowding, narrow entry and exit points, inadequate crowd management and the misleading announcement.The crowd crush, which police said lasted around three minutes, claimed 19 lives and left at least 25 people injured.India is a country of festivals, and its massive religious gatherings also make it prone to stampedes. This year, it was Kolkata.Last year, it was Karur in Tamil Nadu and the Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj. The locations change, the crowds differ, but the tragedy keeps repeating itself.This raises an important question: despite elaborate planning and dedicated crowd management teams, why do stampedes keep happening? And what can authorities do to prevent a small disturbance from turning into a disaster?Public excitement soars during religious gatherings. Actual turnout often exceeds what authorities anticipate, resulting in more people entering an area than it can safely accommodate.As the crowd swells, even a small disturbance, a rumour, someone tripping and falling, a sudden power outage or even a broken barricade can lead to a situation in which people lose control of their movement.According to a 2014 report by the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), titled Managing Crowd at Events and Venues of Mass Gathering: A Guide for State Government, Local Authorities, Administrators and Organizers, crowd disasters can be triggered by several factors.Structural problems such as weak temporary structures, collapsed barricades, poorly lit stairways, slippery roads and narrow entrances and exits can lead to a crowd crush.Fires, electrical failures and security scares can also turn an otherwise manageable gathering into a dangerous crush.The report explains the causes of stampedes through the "FIST" model which is an acronym for Force, Information, Space and Time. According to the model, the four factors that can contribute to a crowd disaster are the force exerted by the crowd, the information that triggers its reaction, the physical space available and the duration of the incident."The FIST circumstances namely crowd force, the information upon which the crowd acts, the physical space involved, and the time duration of the incident play a very important role resulting in either overcrowding or high desired velocity," the report says.In simple terms, when too many people are packed into a limited space, pressure builds as those behind continue moving forward while those in front are unable to move. At extreme crowd densities, people can be pushed against one another with such force that they lose control of their movements. Even those who remain standing can struggle to breathe.Deaths in such situations do not necessarily occur because someone has literally been "trampled" under the feet of others. The NDMA says compressive asphyxia, which occurs when pressure on the chest prevents a person from breathing, has historically been the most common cause of death in crowd disasters."On occasions, this has led to deaths because of crushing, suffocation, and trampling. Historically, compressive asphyxia has been the most common reason for deaths in crowd disasters," the report says.Crowd psychology is also a factor that can contribute to a stampede-like situation. According to the NDMA report, individuals often conform their thoughts and behaviour to those of a larger group rather than acting independently."Individual behaviour in a crowd is sometimes influenced by the behaviour of others. The individuals within a crowd may act differently than if they were on their own," it says."The unlawful actions of a few people can result in larger numbers following them. Research has shown that understanding of crowd behaviour has led to community based approach to crowd control instead of force based control," the report adds.For instance, long queues at places of worship may lead some devotees to climb over fences, prompting others to follow and causing overcrowding in another area.However, crowd behaviour is not always irrational. People react to incomplete information, the movement of others and the fear of danger. In dense crowds, they may also lose the ability to control their own movement.This is why rumours and misleading announcements can be particularly dangerous. People may begin moving towards an exit without knowing what is happening elsewhere in the venue. If the exit is already congested, the sudden movement can increase pressure on those trapped in the crowd.Talking to The Times of India, former Bihar director general of police Abhayanand, who handled several such gatherings during his long service, said police should refrain from using force when a crowd is already panicked during a stampede-like situation."There is always a trigger, however small. It is followed immediately thereafter by a rumour which spreads like wildfire," Abhayanand said."I haven't followed any SOP in my days. I followed two basics: The crowd has panicked. Don't increase the panic by lathi charge. If there is an individual in whom the crowd has trust and if he can be made to communicate with the crowd, its effect is magical," he added."Crowds where there is some common binding force experience stampede. Such stampedes are easier to manage," he further said.Abhayanand also recalled handling a similar situation during the funeral procession of Ranvir Sena chief Brahmeshwar Mukhiya in Patna in 2012. He said police refrained from using force against a particularly unruly gathering of supporters."The crowd was itching for a trigger, and a police lathi charge could have set things off. We restrained ourselves because the repercussions would not have been limited to the capital but could have spread across the entire state," he told TOI."Those indulging in arson wanted the police to react and resort to a lathi charge. That was precisely what they were trying to provoke, but we did not allow that trigger to be pulled," he added.His account points to the importance of police response when a crowd is already on edge. An attempt to disperse people by force can worsen the situation if it causes them to rush towards a narrow exit or move against an incoming crowd.The NDMA has also laid down guidelines on how authorities should manage crowds and respond when a stampede-like situation develops.According to the agency, the guiding principle should be to bridge the gap between demand and supply. This requires controlling the number of people entering a venue, regulating the crowd within it and managing the outflow when necessary.The NDMA recommends designated staging points through which visitors should pass, along with effective systems to count and monitor people moving through them. Multiple routes should be encouraged to prevent bottlenecks and facilitate the movement of vulnerable groups.Crowd management also requires authorities to anticipate disturbances without allowing their response to trigger a larger crisis."Such miscreants should be immediately quarantined and removed. Action should be taken immediately with tact and firmness, without inviting undue attention from the general public, which may be there if force is used," it says."Inappropriate or poorly managed control procedures may precipitate crowd incidents rather than preventing them. For example, police reacting to a group of unruly people may chase them in a direction opposite to the incoming crowd, which may create a collision, and hence a disaster. Special attention should also be given to the border of the venue and the floating crowd moving there because the mischief is usually caused at such places," it adds.The agency also recommends "input control" by restricting or staggering entry to prevent overcrowding. Authorities must be able to regulate, slow or temporarily stop the inflow when a venue reaches its safe capacity.This also means keeping entry and exit routes clear, ensuring that people leaving a venue do not collide with those entering, and monitoring areas where crowds tend to gather or stop moving.Communication is another important part of crowd management. The NDMA says a lack of reliable information can cause people to panic or change direction, leading to dangerous crowd movements."Communicating with visitors and providing them with the correct information is a very critical factor in all situations," the report says, stressing that communication is essential during normal operations, emergencies and recovery.The Kolkata tragedy showed how quickly things can go wrong when these safeguards fail. Police said the crowd had become congested near the exit during the rain, even as the entry point remained open. The misleading announcement about the pandal collapsing is believed to have added to the pressure, although investigators are still examining the exact sequence of events.Ultimately, effective crowd management lies in anticipating pressure, regulating movement and ensuring that a small trigger does not turn into an uncontrollable chain of events. The challenge is not just to prepare for the thousands expected to attend an event, but also to recognise when a gathering is becoming unsafe and act before it is too late.
Article Summary: Stampede at Kolkata pandal during Durga Puja claimed 19 lives. India is a country of festivals, and its massive religious gatherings also make it prone to stampedes. Structural problems such as weak temporary structures, collapsed barricades, poorly lit stairways and narrow entrances and exits can lead to a crowd crush.

Article Title: Glacial lake outburst in Bhutan: North Bengal on red alert as flood threat looms; thousands evacuated
Article Text:
A major Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) occurred on Thursday evening, October 29, 2026, at Shintaphu Lake (also known as Lemthang or Shintaphu Tsho) in the Gasa district of northwestern Bhutan.

West Bengal shifts thousands to safety

Assam monitors possible impact in Dhubri

What is a glacial lake outburst flood?

NEW DELHI: Parts of West Bengal and Assam were placed on high alert after a glacial lake outburst in Bhutan triggered a flash flood, raising fears of a sudden rise in water levels along the Sankosh river. More than 10,000 people have been moved to relief shelters and safer locations in West Bengal, while authorities in Assam's Dhubri district have stepped up preparedness to deal with possible downstream effects.The outburst sent large volumes of water downstream through the Mo Chhu river towards the Sankosh river system, prompting authorities to activate disaster response mechanisms in vulnerable areas.The flood washed away infrastructure at the Gasa Tshachu natural hot springs in Bhutan's Gasa district. No injuries or loss of life have been reported, state broadcaster Bhutan Broadcasting Service (BBS) said on Friday.The full extent of the damage from the late-night flood remained unclear. BBS said the assessment was hampered by “darkness and the strong flow” of floodwaters. Two Bailey bridges, constructed using portable, prefabricated sections, may also have been washed away.According to Bhutan's national newspaper Kuensel, parts of the road leading to Laya village, where the hot springs are located, were washed away, making the route impassable.The road has been closed to traffic indefinitely. The area was evacuated before the floodwaters reached the hot springs.Authorities in West Bengal have alerted residents living along the Sankosh river and its tributaries following reports of the glacial lake outburst flood in Bhutan.Residents in the Darjeeling hills, Terai and Dooars regions have also been advised to remain alert and move to safer locations if they live in vulnerable areas.BJP MP from Darjeeling Raju Bista issued an alert through a post on X on Thursday, urging people living in the catchment areas of the Sankosh river and its connected tributaries to move to safer locations."A glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) has been reported at Lemthang in Bhutan. The overflowing water from the lake is flowing downwards through the Mofu River towards the Sunkosh River," the post read."Therefore, everyone living in the catchment areas of the Sunkosh River and all its connected tributaries have been informed to move to a safe distance immediately to protect their lives. Everyone in our Darjeeling hills, Terai and Dooars region are requested to stay alert," he added.State minister Nisith Pramanik said the government had received reports of the glacial lake outburst and that the overflowing water was moving towards the Sankosh river through the Mo Chhu river."Reports have just come in regarding a glacial lake outburst in Bhutan. Water from the lake is overflowing and flowing downstream into the Mo Chhu River, heading toward the Sankosh River. Residents living along the Sankosh River and its tributaries have been alerted; they are advised to move to a safe distance immediately to ensure their safety," Pramanik said.He said the water was expected to reach the plains within five to six hours, raising concerns about possible flooding."To manage the situation, the State Disaster Management Team has been activated, and the NDRF has also been notified. Disaster management volunteers have been instructed to be present on-site. The government is taking proactive measures and closely monitoring the situation to prevent any loss of life or property," he added.Alipurduar Superintendent of Police Amit Kumar Shaw appealed to residents not to panic, saying the administration was coordinating with Bhutanese authorities and disaster response agencies."First of all, I would like to tell the residents of the district that there is absolutely no need to panic. The situation is currently under control. We are in constant touch with the authorities in Bhutan. Our police team, the District Magistrate (DM) and the Block Development Officer (BDO) with their respective teams, along with all relevant agencies and stakeholders, are working together in close coordination," Shaw told ANI.He said the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) had been deployed in the area, while a National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) team was also on its way. Civil Defence personnel had additionally been mobilised to assist with preparedness measures."We have already moved approximately 4,000 to 5,000 people into shelters, utilising school buildings as relief centres. Additionally, more than 6,000 people have been relocated to safe areas," he said.Shaw said the intensity of the water flow had decreased slightly, according to the latest information received, but the administration remained on high alert."The police, the DM's office, and the BDO's office have made arrangements for dry food and drinking water. We have also ensured that other necessities, such as toilet facilities, are provided. We will wait to see what the situation looks like in two hours. We are fully prepared and ready to handle any emergency that may arise," he said.He added that a red alert was in force for the Sankosh river system and warned that the approaching floodwaters could carry dead fish and debris, including large pieces of wood and concrete."We expect to see water flowing through the Sankosh River, likely accompanied by dead fish, as well as large pieces of wood and concrete debris," Shaw said.Meanwhile, the Assam government said it was closely monitoring the situation following the glacial lake outburst in Bhutan, with Dhubri district placed on alert over possible downstream effects.The Sankosh river flows through Dhubri district, and authorities have stepped up vigilance amid the possibility of a sudden rise in water levels."The situation arising out of the Glacial Lake Outburst Flood in Bhutan is being closely monitored by HCM Dr @himantabiswa," the Chief Minister's Office said in a social media post."Team @dcofficedhubri is on ground and prepared to effectively deal with the downstream effects," it added.An Assam State Disaster Management Authority spokesperson said the water level of the Sankosh river was steady as of 6.30 am on Friday. The district administration and disaster response teams were on alert to tackle any eventuality.A special advisory issued by the ministry of Jal Shakti on Thursday for Assam and West Bengal said the Indian Embassy had reported a GLOF in Shintaphu Lake, located in Bhutan's Punatsangchhu river basin.Following reports of flash floods in the river's upper reaches, water levels in the Sankosh river could rise suddenly in Assam's Dhubri and West Bengal's Alipurduar districts, the advisory said.Local authorities in both districts were advised to remain alert, closely monitor the situation and take necessary precautionary measures.A glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF), also known as a jokulhlaup, occurs when the natural dam holding back a glacial lake fails or is breached, releasing large volumes of water downstream.Such floods can cause sudden destruction of roads, bridges, settlements and other infrastructure, particularly in mountainous regions.Shintaphu Lake, located below Wakila Mountain in Lungo, Laya Gewog, in Bhutan's Gasa district, is among 17 glacial lakes in the country identified as potentially dangerous, according to local reports.Gasa Tshachu, a popular natural hot spring in northern Bhutan, was also hit by a flash flood in 2021 when the Mochhu river changed course and swept through the area.The latest incident has renewed concerns over glacial lake outburst floods in the Himalayan region. In August, a flash flood near Nepal's border with China killed more than 1,500 people and left over 5,000 missing, according to the supplied report.
Article Summary: Glacial lake outburst in Bhutan raises fears of a sudden rise in water levels along the Sankosh river. More than 10,000 people have been moved to relief shelters and safer locations in West Bengal. Authorities in Assam's Dhubri district have stepped up preparedness to deal with possible downstream effects.

Article Title: Indian scholars labelled ‘migrant workers’ in Taiwan social media post, file police complaint over racism
Article Text:
Pic 1: People in a busy street of Taipei.| Pic2: An offensive billboard targeting Indians installed by a local politician in Taiwan early this year. (PC: Suvam Pal/Taipei)





DEHRADUN: Seven Indian research scholars and students in Taiwan filed a police complaint after a photograph of them returning from a Durga Puja celebration in Taipei was circulated on social media with a caption falsely identifying them as ‘Indian migrant workers’ and allegedly targeting them with racist remarks. The students said a Taiwanese man had taken the photograph with their permission on Oct 18, claiming to appreciate Indian culture, but they later found it being used in a post attacking a major political party over Indian migrant workers. The incident prompted members of the Indian diaspora to document similar posts and seek action from Taiwanese authorities.Soumi Panja, 28, a research scholar at National Taiwan University (NTU) for the past three years and one of the seven people in the photograph, told TOI from Taipei on Wednesday night that the man, who appeared to be 55-60 years old, approached them while they were travelling on a metro train after the celebration.“He exchanged greetings with us inside the train while claiming that he used to earlier work as a teacher in Australia before returning to Taiwan to lead retirement life. However, next day, I was informed by one of my friends from the group that our photo is being widely circulated on the local social media with a caption mentioning us a Indian migrant labourers in a racist and offensive caption. We were just shocked to find that because the man had taken us in confidence with a completely opposite claim,” said Panja.She said the group was particularly disturbed because the post used their photograph without authorisation to make a political allegation unrelated to them. After consulting senior members of the Indian community, the seven students approached police on Oct 20 and recorded their statements separately.“We then discussed the incident with our seniors from India and then subsequently decided to lodge a police complaint on Oct 20. Each of the seven in the group recorded their statements before the police separately. The police then registered a case and assured us of appropriate legal action in the stipulated time ranging from one to three months. However, the offensive post with our photographs is still visible on social media and yet to be taken down,” said Panja.Suvam Pal, an Indian media professional who has worked in Taiwan since 2022 and whom the students consulted after the incident, said similar social media posts targeting Indians had appeared earlier. He alleged that some local politicians and individuals had circulated offensive claims portraying Indians as habitual sex offenders.“There have been similar incidents in the past too in which some local politicians and individuals have posted racist and offensive content against Indians by labeling them as habitual sex offenders, which is completely wrong. This recent incident seems to be inspired by certain political elements in the wake of the upcoming local body polls scheduled on Nov 28. Having said that, I can also vouch of Taiwan being only second to Japan in terms of security, professionalism and friendly society, after having travelled over 50 countries so far,” said Pal.Following the incident, Pal and other Indians in Taiwan formed a WhatsApp group, Rage Against Racism, to collect allegedly racist social media posts and prepare a complaint for local authorities.Shubham Roy Chowdhury, another NTU research scholar who has lived in Taiwan since 2023, said the group had identified more than 300 such posts in four to five days.“We observed that it has increased in the last 8-10 months with many of the posts being shared by by handlers sitting in Pakistan and China. We will soon make a report on the posts and submit to the Taiwanese authorities for appropriate action,” said Chowdhury who is among the three Indians running the Whatsapp group.The claim about the origin of these posts could not be independently verified.Cheng Yan Liu, 30, a Taiwanese national who runs Netaji Bose Bharat Cultural Centre in Kaohsiung to ‘educate Taiwanese about India’, also expressed concern. He alleged that “certain elements in a neighbouring country wants to sow discord between Indian and Taiwan for their own geopolitical interests.”“To tackle such activities, both the govts should work on cultural exchange programmes and promoting people to people contact so that they can understand each other’s country in a better way to erase misconceptions and prejudices. Having visited India several times and well aware of the Indian culture, I can claim that India is completely different from what its image has been created on social media,” said Liu.
Article Summary: Seven Indian research scholars and students in Taiwan filed a police complaint after a photograph of them returning from a Durga Puja celebration in Taipei was circulated on social media. The students said a Taiwanese man had taken the photograph with their permission on Oct 18, claiming to appreciate Indian culture. They later found it being used in a post attacking a major political party over Indian migrant workers.

NEW DELHI: Jamia Millia Islamia has set May 15, 2027, as the deadline for approving and implementing its students’ union constitution and decided to revoke disciplinary action against protesting students. The university has also decided to hold students’ union elections within six weeks of the commencement of the next academic session, addressing three key demands raised by students during their 18-day protest seeking the restoration of the elected union, which has remained defunct since 2006.A student said the university had accepted all three demands, including a fixed deadline for implementing the constitution, an election schedule and the withdrawal of disciplinary proceedings against protesters.“Order has come in, it covers 3 points: 1) The approval and implementation of the Jamia Millia Islamia Students’ Union Constitution shall be completed by 15th May, 2027. We had demanded a date and they have announced a date, 2) The elections shall be conducted within 6 weeks of the start of the academic session, that is approximately within 6 weeks from 16 July 2027, 3) All disciplinary actions (taken against protesting students) will be revoked.They have accepted all 3 of our demands...We are calling off our hunger strike and protest...”The decision comes amid mounting tensions on campus over the demand for the restoration of the Jamia Millia Islamia Students’ Union (JMISU). Students had continued their agitation despite an earlier university order stating that elections would be held within 15 days of the approval of the union’s constitution. They had questioned the absence of a deadline for approving the constitution.The administration had also initiated disciplinary proceedings against students during the agitation. On October 27, the provost of Begum Hazrat Mahal Girls’ Hostel issued a show-cause notice to a student for allegedly obtaining emergency leave on misleading grounds and participating in the protest. The student was asked to submit a written explanation within 24 hours.The university has extended online classes until November 24 and shifted odd-semester examinations to online mode, citing the prevailing campus situation and concerns over students’ safety and security.
Article Summary: Jamia Millia Islamia has set May 15, 2027, as the deadline for approving and implementing its students' union constitution. The university has also decided to hold students’ union elections within six weeks of the commencement of the next academic session. A student said the university had accepted all three demands, including a fixed deadline for implementing the constitution.

Article Title: She collected salary for 16 years without teaching: German teacher who allegedly went scuba diving while on sick leave now faces fraud charges over €248,000
Article Text:
How the 16-year absence came under scrutiny

€248,000 in alleged losses and two suspected forged documents

Scuba diving and the limits of the investigation

A 62-year-old German teacher who reportedly remained on paid sick leave for 16 years without returning to the classroom has been charged with fraud and forgery, in a case that has raised questions about oversight of long-term sick leave among civil servants. According to German public broadcaster Tagesschau, citing the Duisburg public prosecutor’s office, the teacher is accused of fraud in 11 particularly serious cases and forging two documents. Investigators allege she received more than €248,000 in salary payments between March 2021 and March 2025 despite being capable of working. The charges were filed at the Regional Court in Duisburg, and the court must now decide whether to open a full trial.The woman, whose identity has not been publicly disclosed, was employed at a vocational college in Wesel, a town in Germany’s North Rhine-Westphalia region. She reportedly stopped teaching in February 2009 but continued receiving her full salary as a civil servant while submitting medical certificates to justify her absence. The case first attracted widespread attention in 2025, when officials sought to establish whether she remained medically unfit to teach.The subsequent criminal investigation has now brought fresh allegations, including the suspected falsification of medical documents connected to her scuba-diving activities.The case came to light after education authorities reviewed the teacher’s personnel file and questioned why she had remained away from work for so many years without undergoing a formal medical assessment. According to earlier reporting by VICE, a new school administrator initiated scrutiny of the arrangement after years of continued salary payments. The teacher challenged an order requiring her to undergo a medical examination, arguing that the demand was unjustified after such a prolonged period of certified illness. A court rejected her challenge and ordered her to pay €2,500 in legal costs, according to earlier reports.The dispute raised questions about why an official medical assessment had not been ordered much earlier. Under the civil-service system, teachers in Germany can receive their full salary while medically unfit for duty, unlike many private-sector employees, whose sickness benefits are subject to time limits.However, the entitlement does not exempt civil servants from medical assessments or disciplinary procedures. Authorities can examine whether an employee remains fit to work and whether retirement on medical grounds is necessary.The latest criminal case concerns payments made between March 2021 and March 2025. According to the Duisburg prosecutor’s office, the teacher allegedly submitted certificates stating that she was unable to work, despite knowing that she was medically capable of performing her duties. Prosecutors allege that these documents persuaded the state of North Rhine-Westphalia, her employer, to continue paying her salary. The payments under investigation total more than €248,000. The charges also include two counts of alleged forgery. Investigators suspect that the woman created two certificates declaring her fitness to scuba dive and presented them as documents issued by a doctor. According to the prosecution, the doctor named in the certificates did not exist.The distinction is important: the documents in question allegedly certified her fitness for diving, rather than her fitness to teach. Investigators are examining them as part of the wider case concerning her prolonged absence from the classroom. The prosecution period is limited to 2021–2025 because earlier potential offences are considered time-barred. The €248,000 figure therefore does not represent the total salary she may have received during her entire absence. Based on estimates reported by The Times, her total earnings over approximately 16 years could have approached €1 million. That figure is an estimate, not the amount covered by the current indictment.The case has attracted attention because the teacher was reportedly an active scuba diver while on sick leave. Prosecutors allege that she forged the two diving-fitness certificates, but the investigation has not established that she was working in another profession during her absence. Earlier reports suggested that she might have operated as a naturopathic practitioner or developed a business selling skin creams. However, Tagesschau reported that investigators could not confirm indications that she had actually pursued other professional employment while on sick leave.The allegations concerning her diving activities and the suspected certificates must therefore be distinguished from claims about a second career. Neither the alleged fraud nor the forgery charges amount to a finding of guilt. The teacher has not publicly responded to the criminal allegations, according to reports. The court has yet to decide whether the indictment will be admitted and a main trial opened.
Article Summary: A 62-year-old German teacher has been charged with fraud and forgery. She reportedly remained on paid sick leave for 16 years without returning to the classroom. Investigators allege she received more than €248,000 in salary payments between March 2021 and March 2025. She is accused of fraud in 11 particularly serious cases and forging two documents.

Article Title: A California couple bought a home with a 20-by-20-foot garden, then a neighbour claimed the land; a 1955 deal involving $250 and babysitting helped secure their exclusive gardening rights in an Octobe
Article Text:
Rupert Clayton and Miriam Pinchuk bought their Oakland home in 2019, unaware that their neighbours would later claim ownership of its garden. (AI image)

A garage, $250 and a babysitting arrangement

How new neighbours became involved

What the court discovered

Why Canada and Rodriguez lost appeal

A small garden became the centre of a legal battle between two California couples after a property survey revealed that the land belonged to a neighbouring house. Rupert Clayton and Miriam Pinchuk had bought their Oakland home in 2019 believing that the 20-by-20-foot garden was included in the property. But their neighbours, Herbert Canada and Bernadette Rodriguez, claimed the land was legally theirs. The dispute eventually reached the California Court of Appeal, which ruled on Monday that Clayton and Pinchuk could continue using the garden exclusively.According to the California Judicial Branch , the disagreement was unusual because the garden had been separated from the neighbouring property for decades. A retaining wall and fence stood between the two homes, making the disputed area appear to be part of Clayton and Pinchuk's backyard. Thick vegetation also made it difficult to access the garden from the other property.When the couple bought their house, the garden was already well maintained. They considered it an important part of their new home and began using it regularly.However, the confusion had begun long before either couple moved into the neighbourhood. The answer to why the garden was enclosed within one property but legally belonged to another lay in an agreement made in 1955.In the 1950s, the two properties belonged to the Reom and Kroeger families. The Kroegers wanted to replace their garage, but their plans would interfere with an alleyway that the Reoms had the right to use.The families eventually reached an arrangement that allowed the construction to go ahead. The Reoms agreed to surrender their alleyway access rights, while the Kroegers agreed to give them a small section of land.The agreement also involved a payment of $250 and babysitting services provided by Carol Reom for the Kroegers' young child.Following the arrangement, the Kroegers built their new garage and put up a retaining wall and fence. The small piece of land was enclosed within the Reom family's backyard, where it remained for decades.Harry and Carol Reom continued using the area as a garden for more than 50 years. But although the two families had reached an agreement, the necessary property records were never properly completed, according to the findings later examined in court.That missing paperwork became important when the houses changed hands and the new owners began questioning where one property ended and the other began.Canada and Rodriguez purchased the Piedmont property in 2017. Two years later, Clayton and Pinchuk bought the adjoining Oakland house from the Reom family trust.Before the second sale, however, Canada had already been in contact with the Reom family over a separate matter.In 2018, he needed permission to connect to a drainage pipe on their property for renovation work. During those discussions, Larry Reom, the son of Harry and Carol, told him about the old land agreement and provided a document describing it.Larry later testified that Canada had indicated he would have the document officially recorded. The Reom family subsequently allowed the drainage connection without asking for payment.The garden issue came up again in 2020, when Clayton and Pinchuk discussed replacing the boundary fence with their neighbours. Canada showed them a survey indicating that the garden was legally part of his property.This came as a surprise to the couple, who had believed that the garden was included in their purchase.The disagreement continued until December 2021, when Canada contacted the police and reported that Clayton and Pinchuk were trespassing. The couple stopped using the garden while they pursued the matter in court.By the time the case went to trial, the people who had made the original arrangement in 1955 were no longer available to explain what had happened. The court therefore had to rely on surviving documents and testimony from family members.Larry Reom said he had seen a written record of the agreement among his parents' papers, but he could not locate it when the case was heard. Other documents, including old correspondence, supported the account that the families had agreed to exchange the garden area for money, babysitting, and the surrender of alleyway access rights.The court also considered how the land had been used since the 1950s. The Reom family had maintained the garden for decades, while the wall and fence had kept it physically separate from the Kroeger property.After hearing the evidence, the trial court decided that Clayton and Pinchuk should be allowed to continue gardening there, even though it could not establish that ownership of the land had been legally transferred.It granted them an equitable easement, a legal right allowing someone to use another person's land for a particular purpose without owning it.Canada and Rodriguez challenged the trial court's decision, arguing that the couple should not have been given exclusive gardening rights over land that legally belonged to them.The appeal required the judges to consider whether allowing Clayton and Pinchuk to keep using the garden would be fair, given the history of the two properties.One important consideration was how much the couple stood to lose. They had bought their home believing that the garden was included and had spent two years developing it. The area also had fertile soil and was among the flattest parts of their backyard.The court found that Canada and Rodriguez had made little use of the disputed land. Their drainage needs had also been addressed through the separate permission granted by the Reom family.The judges considered the 1955 arrangement particularly important because the previous owners of the neighbouring property had already benefited from it by being able to build their garage. The appellate court ultimately agreed with the trial court's assessment and upheld its decision.What are your views on this? Tell us in the comments section below.
Article Summary: Rupert Clayton and Miriam Pinchuk bought their Oakland home in 2019. They believed that the 20-by-20-foot garden was included in the property. But their neighbours, Herbert Canada and Bernadette Rodriguez, claimed the land was legally theirs. The dispute reached the California Court of Appeal, which ruled on Monday that Clayton and Pinchesuk could continue using the garden exclusively.

Article Title: Hasina video, RAW allegations: What ex-Bangladesh officer revealed in podcast before mysterious death
Article Text:
Ex-Bangladesh officer found dead after rejecting allegations of links to RAW

What ex-Bangladesh officer said about allegations

A former Bangladesh air force officer was found dead near Turag River in Dhaka on Wednesday, weeks after his podcast questioning allegations linking him to a video purportedly showing former prime minister Sheikh Hasina fleeing the country in August 2024.The 28-year-old former flight lieutenant Tahsif Souri had gone missing a day before his body was recovered. Police said an inquest report found no external injury marks on his body, though blood was seen coming out of his nose.His body was sent to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College for an autopsy.Souri had been "compulsorily retired" from service about a year after the fall of the Hasina government.His death has brought renewed attention to a podcast interview in which he spoke about allegations that he had recorded and circulated footage of Hasina leaving Bangladesh on August 5, 2024.The interview resurfaced following the recovery of his body.During the interview as cited by the Dhaka Tribune, the host referred to a media report alleging that footage of Hasina leaving the country had been recorded at Kurmitola Airport and circulated by Souri. The report had also reportedly linked him to an investigation into the alleged involvement of the Research and Analysis Wing (RAW), within the Bangladesh air force.Responding to the allegations, Souri said the report had claimed that flight lieutenant Rifat Ashrafi recorded the video and that he had circulated it. He questioned the evidence behind the claim that he had shared the footage.“Even if I recorded the video or circulated it, what proof do they have? I want to ask that,” he said.Asked whether the allegations had led to his dismissal from the air force, Souri said this was possible but declined to disclose details of the events at the time.“I cannot disclose everything, and there are things I am unable to discuss. I think they did this because of these allegations,” he said.Souri also said he faced social embarrassment and harassment after the report was published, claiming its headline and presentation had created a misleading impression of him among readers.He rejected allegations of RAW's involvement within the air force, saying: “If I were linked to RAW, why would I be in Bangladesh? If I were linked to RAW, why would I speak publicly?”He described the allegation as “a very ridiculous claim”.Souri further claimed that the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) directorate had said he had no such involvement. However, no detailed documents supporting the claim were presented during the interview.Asked whether he had appealed against his discharge from the air force, Souri said he had not and was uncertain whether he would do so in the future.He also expressed frustration over the withholding of his passport, describing it as a violation of his democratic rights.“They had withheld my passport, which is my democratic right. I am deeply upset about this. I suffered for two years,” he said, adding that he had since recovered the passport.Souri's interview prompted the military's public relations directorate, ISPR, to reiterate its August 4, 2025, statement. It had denied reports that action against Souri and flight lieutenant Rifat Ashrafi was linked to allegations that the officers had recorded and shared the video showing Hasina fleeing the country.During the podcast, Souri dismissed as propaganda a 2024 media report claiming he was an agent of RAW. However, he neither confirmed nor denied his alleged links to the video.Souri's father, KM Enayetul Karim Helal, told reporters that an acquaintance, Dwip, had taken his son out on Tuesday evening."Tahsif sent his mother a message round 1:30am Wednesday, saying he would return home. But he never did" said Helal.Bangladesh home minister Salahuddin Ahmed told reporters that he would comment after the initial probe and autopsy findings. He did not respond when asked whether Souri had shot the video.Meanwhile, Ashraful Alam Khokan, a former aide of Hasina, questioned whether Souri had been deliberately targeted through media reports."Was Tahsif deliberately portrayed in the media as an agent of RAW with the intention of getting him killed? "At the time, however, his activities were reportedly aligned with those who seized power in July," he said, referring to the Muhammad Yunus-led government.
Article Summary: Tahsif Souri, 28, was found dead near Turag River in Dhaka on Wednesday. Police said an inquest report found no external injury marks on his body, though blood was seen coming out of his nose. His death has brought renewed attention to a podcast interview in which he spoke about allegations that he had recorded and circulated footage of Hasina leaving Bangladesh.

Article Title: Jamia set to hold student body polls after 22 years; 18-day hunger strike ends
Article Text:
Students celebrate after their demands are accepted

Polls at Jamia likely in Aug next year, 18-day hunger strike ends





NEW DELHI: After over two decades without an elected students' union, Jamia Millia Islamia (JMI) is set to return to campus democracy, with the university committing to complete the union constitution by May 15, 2027, and hold elections by Aug 27, 2027. The last union election was held in 2005, reports Sugandha Jha.The breakthrough came late Thursday after registrar Md Mahtab Alam Rizvi visited the protest site around 9pm and held talks with the agitating students, bringing the 18-day hunger strike to an end on the university's 106th Foundation Day. The registrar's order, issued after the discussions, addressed the protesters' central demand for a time-bound roadmap to restore elected student representation. It also directed the withdrawal of disciplinary action linked to the stir.The five hunger strikers ended their fast with juice offered by the registrar. Celebrations broke out at the protest site after the order to complete union polls and constitution was issued.The order stated: “The approval and implementation of the Jamia Millia Islamia Students’ Union Constitution shall be completed by May 15, 2027.Subsequent to the approval of the Constitution, the university shall release the notification for elections in accordance with the recommendations and guidelines of the Lyngdoh Committee. This date will be in accordance with the guidelines set forth by the Lyngdoh Committee regulations. The elections shall be conducted within six weeks of the start of the academic session, i.e., approximately within six weeks from July 16, 2027.”On disciplinary proceedings, the administration directed: “All ongoing show-causes notices, disciplinary actions, rustications, suspensions and campus ban orders issued in connection with participation in the protest period shall be revoked.”“In view of the above, the protesting students shall call off their hunger strike with immediate effect,” it added.The resolution came on a day when JMI’s customary Foundation Day celebrations were curtailed amid the agitation. Instead of the usual programme, the official observance was limited to flag hoisting and the university anthem, while protesting students organised an ‘Inquilabi Mela’ at Gulistan-e-Ghalib near Gate No. 7. Hunger strikers Ebin Basil and Rehan Khan were designated ‘chief guests’ at the parallel event, which featured speeches and the release of a protest report and memorandum.Jamia traditionally marks its foundation day with weeklong celebrations attended by prominent dignitaries. Last year, Union minister Kiren Rijiju was the chief guest. This year, the agitation overshadowed the occasion, turning it into a platform for students to press for democratic representation.How the standoff escalatedThe agitation began on Oct 12, with students demanding the restoration of the Jamia Millia Islamia Students’ Union (JMISU), which has remained defunct since 2006. On Oct 24, the administration issued an order accepting the protesters’ demands and stating elections would be held within 15 days of approval of the students’ union constitution after the agitation grew bigger and gained support from political figures. However, the order did not specify a deadline for completing the constitution, leaving a key procedural step open-ended and failing to address the protesters’ demand for a time-bound roadmap.The movement intensified as five students — Ebin Basil, Rehan Khan, Ritik, Altaf and Abuzar — began an indefinite hunger strike. Their demands also included the release of students in police custody and Tihar Jail, withdrawal of show-cause notices issued to female students, and removal of the chief proctor and security adviser.The standoff subsequently saw clashes between students and security personnel, increased security deployment, restrictions on campus gatherings and a shift to online classes. Protesters also faced disciplinary proceedings, campus-ban orders and directions for some students to leave the campus. The university is now expected to resume physical classes soon.
Article Summary: Jamia Millia Islamia (JMI) is set to return to campus democracy. University to complete union constitution by May 15, 2027, and hold elections by Aug 27. Last union election was held in 2005. 18-day hunger strike ends on university's 106th Foundation Day.

Article Title: Alert sounded in Bengal's Alipurduar after Bhutan lake outburst
Article Text:
Shintaphu Lake, located below Wakila Mountain in Lungo, Laya Gewog, Gasa, experienced an outburst on Thursday evening, according to local reports.





KOLKATA: Bengal forest minister Manoj Oraon late Thursday alerted residents living along the Sankosh river in Alipurduar’s Kumargram area after reports of an outburst from Shintaphu Lake in Bhutan’s Gasa district.The lake lies in the Mo Chhu catchment, which forms part of the Sankosh river system downstream.In a message, Oraon urged residents of Kumargram tea estate, Kumargram forest village, Pakriguri and Bholka to remain alert to rising water levels in the Sankosh and warned of possible flash floods.Shintaphu Lake, located below Wakila Mountain in Lungo, Laya Gewog, Gasa, experienced an outburst on Thursday evening, according to local reports.The reports said people in the affected area had been moved to safer ground. Locals were expected to assess any livestock losses on Friday.Shintaphu Lake is considered one of 17 potentially dangerous glacial lakes. It lies in the upper reaches of the Mo Chhu river basin.
Article Summary: Shintaphu Lake, located below Wakila Mountain in Lungo, Laya Gewog, Gasa, experienced an outburst on Thursday evening. Bengal forest minister Manoj Oraon late Thursday alerted residents living along the Sankosh river in Alipurduar’s Kumargram area.

Article Title: Asked for extra serving of chole, Delhi man stabbed to death by vendor
Article Text:
The victim, Sandeep, who worked as a driver, is survived by his wife and two children. (AI Image)





NEW DELHI: A dispute over an extra serving of chole allegedly turned fatal after a roadside food vendor stabbed a 35-year-old man to death in outer Delhi’s Nihal Vihar, police said.The victim, Sandeep , who worked as a driver, is survived by his wife and two children.According to police, the incident took place Sunday night near Jwalapuri Nala, where Sandeep had ordered a plate of chole-bhature from a roadside stall run by Chintu Gupta. An argument allegedly broke out after Sandeep asked for additional chole and Gupta refused. The disagreement escalated into a physical altercation.Police alleged that Gupta then pulled out a knife from his cart and stabbed Sandeep multiple times.The injured man was initially taken to Sanjay Gandhi Memorial Hospital, where a medico-legal case was registered. Doctors recorded three stab wounds on the left side of his abdomen, three lacerated injuries on his left forearm and another injury on his wrist.Based on the MLC and statements of eyewitnesses, police registered a case and launched an investigation.Sandeep was later shifted to Maharaja Agrasen Hospital in Punjabi Bagh, where he succumbed to his injuries Tuesday.A senior police officer said the victim’s family initially suspected that four to five people had attacked him, but the claim was not supported by eyewitness accounts.The accused, Chintu Gupta, a resident of Nihal Vihar, was arrested and later remanded to judicial custody.The FIR, initially registered under provisions relating to attempt to murder, was amended to include Section 103 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) after the victim’s death. Further investigation is underway.
Article Summary: A dispute over an extra serving of chole allegedly turned fatal after a roadside food vendor stabbed a 35-year-old man to death. The victim, Sandeep, who worked as a driver, is survived by his wife and two children. The accused, Chintu Gupta, a resident of Nihal Vihar, was arrested and later remanded to judicial custody.

Article Title: A friend's girlfriend, a rape allegation, a midnight kidnapping: How Bengaluru techie became target of a revenge plot
Article Text:
Manjunath's friend Mahendra





BENGALURU: City police have arrested 11 people, including a 21-year-old woman, for allegedly kidnapping a 23-year-old techie and his housemate and demanding a ransom of Rs 10 lakh. The techie, rescued along with his friend from a rented house in Nagarabhavi Wednesday afternoon, has also been arrested after the woman accused him of rape.The techie, Bursu Mahendra alias B Mahendra, a native of Madanapalle in Andhra Pradesh, lived in Munnekolalu. Police said the woman’s rape complaint emerged during the investigation into the kidnapping, leading to a separate criminal case against Mahendra.According to investigators, Mahendra was a close friend of Marripati Manjunath alias Manja, who also lived in Munnekolalu. Mahendra was acquainted with Galeti Rajkumar alias Raj, 24, as well.Police said Raj had brought his girlfriend to Manjunath’s house on the night of Oct 24, when Manjunath was away. Mahendra and his housemate Tarun allegedly entered the house around midnight and found Raj with the woman. According to an investigating officer, the two men allegedly assaulted the woman sexually, with Tarun locking Raj in a room while Mahendra allegedly raped her in another room.The two men fled after Manjunath returned home, police said.Deciding to teach the two men a lesson, Rajkumar along with Manjunath mobilised others to kidnap Mahendra and Tarun. Police said the group barged into Mahendra’s house around 2am Wednesday and abducted both men. They allegedly confined them in a room at a rented house in Nagarabhavi before Rajkumar called Mahendra’s father, Ramana, and demanded Rs 10 lakh for their release.Ramana, who was in Madanapalle, was allegedly told to bring the money and wait near Hoskote bus stand. He rushed to Bengaluru and approached Marathahalli police, who launched a probe.Whitefield DCP Saidulu Adavat said special teams were formed to trace the suspects and rescue the hostages. “Using digital clues and information from locals, our teams traced the hideout, rescued the two men, and arrested the accused,” he said.The 11 arrested for kidnapping are Rajkumar, Manjunath, Loknath, Suhail, Narendra Reddy, Shiva Subramanyam, Saleem Pasha, Nayeem Pasha, Shabaz, Rajesh, and the woman.A senior police officer said investigators learnt about the woman’s rape allegation only after the arrests. Cops are now investigating both the alleged sexual assault and the kidnap-for-ransom case.
Article Summary: Bursu Mahendra, a 23-year-old techie, was rescued along with his friend from a rented house in Nagarabhavi Wednesday afternoon. Police said the woman’s rape complaint emerged during the investigation into the kidnapping, leading to a separate criminal case.

Article Title: SC upholds Telangana’s claim over 550 acres prime land worth Rs 25K crore in Miyapur
Article Text:
The Hyderabad Metro Rail depot at Miyapur is also part of the land parcel.





HYDERABAD: In a big win for Telangana govt in a 23-year-old legal battle, Supreme Court on Thursday dismissed a batch of appeals filed by private individuals claiming over 550 acres of prime land at Miyapur, upholding the then AP high court’s finding and the decision of the special court for land grabbing cases that the land belongs to the state.According to sources, the land parcel (in survey numbers 100 & 101) in Miyapur abuts the National Highway-65. Incidentally, the Hyderabad Metro Rail depot at Miyapur is part of the land parcel, valued at over Rs 25,000 crore.“We find no perversity in the findings recorded by both the special court and the high court on this aspect,” a Supreme Court bench, comprising Justice MM Sundresh and Justice Satish Chandra Sharma, said.The court said it saw no reason to invoke equity, describing the matter as "a clear-cut case of attempts being made to grab valuable land vested in the state”. Since the appellants’ own title was lacking, "there was no question of granting equitable relief”, the bench held.Writing the judgments for the bench, Justice Sundresh noted that the land parcels were classified as 'sarkari poramboke’ after the 1912 survey.Miyapur later formed part of a Paigah jagir restored to one Rafi-un-nisa Begum on the recommendation of the Justice Reilly Commission (which inquired into the settlement of Paigah estates) and confirmed by the 1929 ‘firman (farman)’ by the Nizam.The court, however, held that a jagir was a grant of rights in respect of land revenue, not of title, and that the firman itself restricted sale, mortgage or gift without the Nizam’s sanction.Whatever limited rights existed were extinguished by the AP (Telangana Area) (Abolition of Jagirs) Regulation, in force from Aug 15, 1949, under which jagirs were included in the ‘Diwani’ and the jagirdars’ powers and rights had ceased.The court explained that a jagirdar’s entitlement after abolition was confined to the commutation sum, a one-time payment in the nature of compensation. It added that the exceptions for home farms and personal property under Regulations 17 and 18 apply only if proved, and the burden lies on the person asserting them.The judges found the revenue entries pertaining to the land naming Rafi-un-nisa Begum as pattadar in the 1950s pahanies "bogus and not genuine”, the product of fraud in collusion with revenue officials.They further refused to consider a plea raised by the appellants, for the first time in Supreme Court, that the land was bought at an auction in 1918 and bequeathed to Rafi-un-nisa Begum by will in 1943-44.It said the documents had not passed the tests of admissibility, relevancy and proof, were never mentioned in the Reilly Commission (which inquired into the settlement of Paigah estates and the inter se claims) report or any earlier proceeding, and contradicted a century of public state records. The apex court also found that adverse possession was neither proved nor available.Even assuming the land was settled on their predecessor under the 1929 firman, the court said, it conveyed no title and any interest was extinguished by the Abolition Regulation.As Rafi-un-nisa Begum herself lacked a valid title, she could not have passed it to the appellants. The plea that the land was “Zat Jagir” (personally granted property) was rightly rejected, as it was never raised before the special court and no evidence was led on it.The court further noted that some appellants before it were not parties before the special court or high court.The bench also took note of transfer of some of the land parcels to the Hyderabad Urban Development Authority (now HMDA) , but declined to go into the inter se disputes among the claimants.Reacting to the development, the chief minister’s office (CMO) in an official release stated: “A special initiative by chief minister A Revanth Reddy led to the resolution of the Miyapur case pending for 23 years.” The CM directed officials to expedite legal proceedings to protect these highly valuable govt land parcels, it added.BOXGovt records from 1912 listed the land as state property. In the 1920s, the Nizam restored the village to the Paigah family, but only with limited rights. When the Nizam’s old estates were abolished in 1949, the land passed to the state, and the Paigah heirs accepted compensation. Decades later, other claimants surfaced, relying on revenue entries in another heir’s name. In 1997, the special court for land-grabbing cases ruled the land belonged to the state. In 2003, the then Andhra Pradesh high court upheld this, declaring the claimants land grabbers. The private parties challenged high court’s verdict by moving the Supreme Court.
Article Summary: Supreme Court on Thursday dismissed a batch of appeals filed by private individuals claiming over 550 acres of prime land at Miyapur. The court said it saw no reason to invoke equity, describing the matter as "a clear-cut case of attempts being made to grab valuable land vested in the state"

Article Title: 3 siblings found dead in flat near Mumbai; trio recorded video before tragedy
Article Text:
Residents alerted police after noticing a strong foul smell coming from the flat.





VIRAR: Three unmarried siblings were found dead inside their rented flat in the Global City area of Virar (West) on Thursday, with police suspecting they died by suicide after consuming poison.In a video recorded before their deaths, they reportedly cited illness and financial difficulties, police said.The deceased were identified as Kumar Mehta (50), Dipesh Mehta (52) and Khevana Mehta (48). They lived in flat No. 1203 in the D wing of Garden Avenue in Global City. Residents alerted police after noticing a strong foul smell coming from the flat.Bolinj police reached the spot and broke open the door around 2.30am on Thursday. The bodies were found in a decomposed state inside the flat.According to police, the siblings had been living in the rented flat since 2025. One of them had suffered paralysis, while one of the brothers was undergoing treatment for cancer.In the video recorded in Gujarati before their deaths, they reportedly spoke about their health problems and financial distress.Senior inspector Prakash Kawale of Bolinj police station said the siblings may have died three to four days before their bodies were discovered. Their bodies have been sent for postmortem examination.Police also contacted the siblings’ sister, who told investigators that the three were facing financial difficulties and had sought money from her as well.
Article Summary: Three unmarried siblings were found dead inside their rented flat in the Global City area of Virar (West) on Thursday. Residents alerted police after noticing a strong foul smell coming from the flat. Police suspect they died by suicide after consuming poison. In a video recorded before their deaths, they reportedly cited illness and financial difficulties.

Article Title: TVK leader Christopher arrested for sexually harassing college student after offering lift
Article Text:
TVK leader Christopher





KANYAKUMARI: A functionary of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) was arrested on Thursday for allegedly sexually harassing a college student after offering her a lift home in Tamil Nadu’s Kanyakumari district, police said.Christopher, a member of the party’s central district executive committee, had been absconding since a case was registered against him. He hails from Marundhukottai near Thuckalay.The complainant, a second-year college student from Kulasekaram, studies at a private college in Nagercoil. She regularly travelled with another student from Moolachal, who is also a TVK member, police sources said.On the day of the incident, the two students were waiting for a bus after college when it began raining. Christopher, who knew the other student, stopped his car and offered to drop them home, saying he was travelling in the same direction.After dropping the other student at Moolachal, Christopher continued towards Kulasekaram with the complainant, assuring her that he would drop her near her home, police said.The student alleged that Christopher stopped the vehicle along the way and sexually harassed her. She confronted him and tried to get out of the car to escape, according to police sources. He later dropped her near her residence and fled.The student informed her parents after reaching home and subsequently told her college friend about the incident. The two then approached Thuckalay police station and lodged a complaint.Further investigation is under way.
Article Summary: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) functionary arrested for allegedly sexually harassing a college student. Christopher, a member of the party’s central district executive committee, had been absconding since a case was registered against him.

Article Title: Ex-Congress worker shot at, dragged out of car, attacked with sharp weapons in Ludhiana
Article Text:
The accused allegedly fired five to six rounds, following, Jagjot suffered splinter injury near his eye.





LUDHIANA: A group of assailants allegedly fired multiple shots at a property dealer and former Congress worker in Dholewal late Wednesday night when he was with his mother and three-year-old son.The victim, Jagjot Singh, sustained a splinter injury near his eye before the attackers allegedly assaulted him with a sharp-edged weapon and fled.Singh, a resident of Miller Gunj, managed to drive away with his mother and son despite the attack and reach Civil Hospital, where he received treatment.Singh said the family had ordered food while sitting in the car. When he stepped out to make a payment and buy a bottle of water, around eight assailants arrived and opened fire at him.He rushed back into the car, but the accused allegedly tried to pull him out and attacked him with sharp-edged weapons. As he resisted and attempted to drive away, they fired several rounds at the car, shattering its windowpanes.Singh alleged that he knew the attackers and claimed the same people had attacked his house and opened fire about a year ago over a rivalry.He also alleged a political angle, saying he was previously associated with the Congress but was no longer affiliated with any political party.He claimed the attackers belonged to another political party and held a grudge against him over electoral rivalry.ACP (Industrial Area-B) Anubhav Jain said police had identified the accused, who allegedly had a rivalry with Singh over their previous political associations. The main accused was identified as Jaswinder Singh, who was accompanied by his aides. An FIR has been registered.
Article Summary: Jagjot Singh, a property dealer and former Congress worker, was with his mother and three-year-old son. When he stepped out to make a payment and buy a bottle of water, around eight assailants arrived and opened fire at him. He sustained a splinter injury near his eye before the attackers allegedly assaulted him with a sharp-edged weapon.

Article Title: 6 dead in MP: 2 sisters, one 8 months pregnant, and 4 children found in separate wells
Article Text:
Two sisters from Madhya Pradesh committed suicide by jumping into wells with their children on Wednesday.





BHOPAL: Two sisters, one of whom was eight months pregnant, allegedly jumped into wells with their four children in two separate incidents in Madhya Pradesh’s Shivpuri district on Wednesday, leaving all six dead.Anjali Rawat, 35, allegedly jumped into a well with her six-year-old son, Prashant, in Gungargaon village, under Bairad police station limits, around 1pm. Hours later, her elder sister, Sita Rawat, 40, was found dead with her three children — Rakhi, 14, Priyanka, 11, and Shlok, 6 — in a well in Khonkar village, under Kolaras police station limits.Police are investigating the two incidents separately and are yet to establish the reasons behind the deaths.Anjali’s three daughters were also present when she allegedly jumped into the well with her son. Her eldest daughter, Monika, rescued herself and her two younger sisters before returning home and informing family members. Relatives rushed to the spot and pulled Anjali and Prashant out of the well, but both had died. Anjali’s unborn child also died.According to family members, Anjali’s husband, Dharmveer Singh Rawat, died in a road accident around one-and-a-half months ago.Police are examining the circumstances surrounding the incident.Sita, a resident of Sesai village, had gone to a field in Khonkar village with her three children. When they had not returned home by around 6pm, relatives began searching for them.They found slippers near a well and spotted a child’s body inside, following which they alerted the police. Kolaras police retrieved the bodies of Sita and her three children by around 11pm.Family members said the sisters were close and frequently spoke to each other over the phone. They suspect Sita may have been affected by Anjali’s death earlier that day, but police have not established any link between the two incidents.Postmortem examinations of all six deceased were scheduled for Thursday. Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding both incidents.
Article Summary: Two sisters from Madhya Pradesh committed suicide by jumping into wells with their children on Wednesday. Anjali Rawat, 35, allegedly jumped into a well with her six-year-old son, Prashant, in Gungargaon village, under Bairad police station limits, around 1pm. Hours later, her elder sister, SitaRawat, 40, was found dead with her three children in a well in Khonkar village. Police are investigating the two incidents separately.

A deadly shooting occurred at Hotel Bilas Inn in Guwahati, leaving five people dead and one injured.

Accused arrested, licensed pistol seized

Congress raises law and order concerns

GUWAHATI: A dispute over a hotel lease allegedly escalated into a deadly shooting in Guwahati on Monday night, leaving five people dead and another injured.The victims included the hotel's co-owner, her son and daughter-in-law, her brother and the property’s caretaker.The accused, identified as Ghanakanta Gogoi, the hotel's leaseholder, was arrested within an hour of the incident, police said.Gogoi allegedly opened fire at Hotel Bilas Inn on GS Road, opposite Bora Service, around 9pm. The hotel is about 2km from the Assam Police headquarters.The victims were associated with the hotel's ownership and management. Four of the deceased belonged to the same family, while the fifth person was from their village, Guwahati police commissioner Partha Sarathi Mahanta said. The injured survivor was also from the same village.“Preliminary investigation suggests that the incident stemmed from a property dispute related to the lease agreement of the hotel,” Mahanta told reporters outside the property.Gogoi had taken the hotel on lease about a year ago, the commissioner said, adding that investigators were examining all aspects of the incident to establish the sequence of events.Police apprehended Gogoi in the Paltan Bazar area within an hour of the shooting.A licensed .32-bore pistol, suspected to have been used in the killings, was seized from him.“Six persons sustained gunshot wounds, of whom five succumbed to the injuries. One person is undergoing treatment,” Mahanta said.Three of the deceased have been identified as Helena Bharali, Deborshi Kashyap and Narayan Das, while the identities of the remaining victims were being verified.The sole survivor, identified as Satyen Pathak, 42, sustained a bullet injury to his shoulder and was undergoing treatment at Gauhati Medical College and Hospital. Police said further investigation would establish the precise circumstances that led to the shooting.Assam Congress president and Jorhat MP Gaurav Gogoi expressed grief over the killings and raised concerns about public safety in Guwahati.In a social media post, Gogoi offered condolences to the victims' families and said the incident raised serious questions about the city's law and order situation. AMRITSAR: The son of an Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) sarpanch was shot dead and his friend was injured when assailants opened fire on them outside a gurdwara in Cheete Kalan village, falling under Chatiwind police station, on Monday evening.The victim, Teerath Singh, was returning after paying obeisance at the gurdwara along with his friend Ranjit Singh when the assailants allegedly opened indiscriminate fire, leaving both injured.Teerath was rushed to a hospital, where doctors declared him brought dead, officials said.Yadwinder Singh, Deputy superintendent of police (DSP), Attari, said that Ranjit, who sustained a bullet injury, is undergoing treatment and is stated to be out of danger.The preliminary investigations suggested that the murder stemmed from an old animosity over a land dispute, the DSP said while ruling out any political rivalry.He further said police have identified four persons, Gurditt Singh, Gurjant Singh, Harkirat Singh alias Hockey, and Gora, and registered an FIR naming them, but no arrests have been made so far.The DSP said that teams have been constituted to investigate the case and arrest the accused.Police sources also informed that the family of Teerath also suspects the involvement of a rival group from the village behind the incident.Notably, Teerath’s brother Karaj Singh had won the sarpanch election on an AAP ticket.The killing triggered a political attack on the AAP government, with former union minister Ravneet Singh Bittu questioning its ability to maintain law and order in Punjab.In a X post, he said, “The murder of Teerath Singh, brother of an incumbent AAP sarpanch, outside a gurdwara in Amritsar is a stark indictment of Punjab’s collapsed law and order.
