Article Title: An Indiana mother was ordered to pay $21,020 in attorney fees amid a custody dispute, then told that no further hearings would be held until she paid; an appeals court ruled on October 28 that the res
Article Text:
Representational image generated using AI

A custody battle that began more than five years ago

Attorney fees piled up

An Indiana appeals court ruled on Wednesday, October 28, that a trial judge cannot stop a custody case from moving forward simply because a parent has not paid legal fees. In a memorandum decision , the appeals court upheld the fee orders against the mother but struck down the condition that barred all further hearings until she paid the $21,020 in attorney fees.The custody battle began in 2021, when the father filed a paternity action concerning his two young children. The children were born out of wedlock in July 2017 and November 2018. The parents lived together until February 2020. That August, the father faced a criminal case over alleged domestic violence against the mother, and a criminal court barred him from contacting her and the children.The father filed for paternity in February 2021. About five months later, on July 26, the court confirmed that he was the children's father. It granted the mother sole legal and primary physical custody while the proceedings continued. It also granted the father supervised parenting time and ordered him to pay child support. In April 2022, the parties agreed to increase the father's unsupervised parenting time in stages. However, in November or December 2022, the mother took the children and left the court's jurisdiction, and their whereabouts became unknown.The father filed a contempt petition, and the children's guardian ad litem recommended that he be granted emergency custody. In January 2023, the judge ruled that the mother's behaviour had endangered the children and constituted a material change in circumstances. The father was granted temporary custody, while the mother was found in indirect contempt and allowed supervised visits.The court also found that the mother was a flight risk and posed a danger to the children's emotional well-being. She was ordered to undergo a psychological evaluation and anger-management assessments, and to complete the recommended treatment before she could progress towards unsupervised visits with her children. The mother was ordered to repay $1,448.34 in child support overpayments and pay $208 a week. The father was granted sole custody in February 2024.About four months later, the father filed a contempt petition. He said the mother had not paid child support as ordered by the court and requested sanctions, including attorney fees. The court ordered the mother to pay the father $10,000 as a sanction. Later that year, she was also ordered to pay another $1,500 for contempt of court orders. Her child support arrears reached $11,708.34.The mother later approached the court seeking to change custody and child support arrangements. The trial court said her July 2024 request to change custody, parenting time and child support was “bordering on the frivolous”, as she had only recently started transitioning to supervised, in-person visits. In March 2026, the court ordered her to pay $15,000 in preliminary fees. She also owed $6,020 in sanctions for unpaid child support, a deposition she had cancelled at the last minute and a motion she had withdrawn just before a hearing.The court was not convinced by the mother's financial claims. She could not provide an exact figure for her income, but the court estimated it at $30,000 to $40,000 a year. It also pointed to a $70,000 settlement she had received, financial assistance from family members and the fact that her landlord was her own mother. The court said it found her income and expenses difficult to reconcile and concluded that she had the ability to pay both her fees and her child support.The trial court also ruled that it would not schedule any further hearings until the mother paid the attorney fees. Following this decision, the mother appealed the fee awards and the suspension of further hearings. The appeals court ruled that the trial court could not make further hearings conditional on the mother paying the attorney fees. It said such awards are money judgments and must be enforced through ordinary collection procedures under Indiana Trial Rule 69, rather than through contempt powers or by blocking access to further hearings. The appeals court reversed the part of the trial court's order that halted hearings until the mother paid the attorney fees. However, it did not overturn the $21,020 fee award. The father can still seek a money judgment and pursue appropriate collection proceedings to recover the amount.
Article Summary: The custody battle began in 2021, when the father filed a paternity action concerning his two young children. The mother was ordered to repay $1,448.34 in child support overpayments and pay $208 a week. In March 2026, the court ordered her to pay $15,000 in preliminary fees. She also owed $6,020 in sanctions for unpaid child support, a deposition she cancelled at the last minute and a motion she had withdrawn just before a hearing.

Article Title: ‘My car is registered in UP, not on another planet’
Article Text:
Govt and private offices have also been directed to reduce staff strength by 50% from Nov 1 to Jan 31, 2027 (AI Image)

GHAZIABAD

From Nov 1 to Jan 31, vehicles registered outside Delhi that do not meet BS-VI emission standards will be barred from entering the capital.For thousands who live in neighbouring cities but work in Delhi, the ban raises practical questions: How do you get to work, pick up a family member from IGI Airport late at night or reach a hospital in an emergency when your own car cannot cross the border? As TOI’s Ishita Jairath finds out, citizens are worried. And confused DMRC has added 20 weekday trips since Oct 22, after Stage-I of GRAP was invoked. “Additional trips have been introduced to encourage more people to use public transport than their personal vehicles. After Stage-II of GRAP comes into effect, 20 more trips will be added, taking the total additional trips to 40,” a DMRC official said.The metro has seen record demand during severe pollution episodes. On Nov 18, 2024, it recorded its then-highest passenger boarding, at 78.7 lakh, as Delhi’s AQI reached 494.Govt and private offices have also been directed to reduce staff strength by 50% from Nov 1 to Jan 31, 2027.Over 10+ lakh vehicles (personal and commercial) are set to go off roads4 lakh+4 lakh2 lakhCNG and electric vehicles, along with specified emergency and sovereign-duty vehicles, such as ambulances, fire tenders and police vehicles.The transport department will deploy 300 enforcement personnel to implement the ban. Automatic number plate recognition cameras, already installed at petrol pumps, will also be used to scan registration plates.Sources claim emergencies will be kept in mind during enforcement.
Article Summary: Vehicles registered outside Delhi that do not meet BS-VI emission standards will be barred from entering the capital. Govt and private offices have also been directed to reduce staff strength by 50% from Nov 1 to Jan 31, 2027. DMRC has added 20 weekday trips since Oct 22.

Article Title: MPSC probe hearings open to public; anyone with related info urged to step forward: Mundhe
Article Text:
Mundhe said the first meeting of the commission had already taken place, and it was decided to keep all hearings open to the public in the spirit of transparency

Mumbai:





All hearings of the Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) inquiry commission will be open to the public at the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) headquarters in BKC, Bandra East, said FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe on Thursday. He also said the panel’s office has been established on the second floor, room 201, within the FDA building itself, and urged anyone with further information in this case to approach the commission.While speaking to the press, he said the first meeting of the commission had already taken place, and it was decided to keep all hearings open to the public in the spirit of transparency. Mundhe said, “Any individuals, candidates, and students possessing relevant information about this case can submit their statements through an affidavit to the commission on or before November 16.”He said candidates can submit statements in either English or Marathi along with a copy of identification documents and self-attested documents. A copy needs to be sent via email to complaints.inquirycomm.mpsc@maharashtra.gov.in.Mundhe said, “Affidavits and documents submitted in response to the Commission’s public notice will be treated as confidential. The Commission will scrutinise the submissions and retain the discretion to decide whether the persons concerned should be examined as witnesses before it.”Govt appointed this commission earlier this month in light of protests by MPSC aspirants following paper-leak allegations in Pune that had spilled over for more than 10 days. This commission is headed by Justice Dilip Bhosale, retired Chief Justice of the Allahabad High Court, and Mundhe is a member secretary.The commission will investigate malpractice and leakage of question papers or answer key leaks in various competitive examinations conducted by the MPSC between 2023 and 2026.The scope of the commission’s inquiry covers the following nine examinations, listed with their advertisement numbers: Drug Inspector Examination Group-B, 2025 (116/2025); Maharashtra Group-B (Non-Gazetted) Services Combined Preliminary Examination, 2025 (117/2025); Maharashtra Group-B (Non-Gazetted) Services Combined Main Examination, 2025 (010/2026); Maharashtra Group-C Services Combined Preliminary Examination, 2025 (124/2025); Maharashtra Group-C Services Main Examination, 2025 (014/2026); Maharashtra Agriculture Services Main Examination, 2024 (055/2025); Food and Drugs Administrative Services Main Examination, 2023 (125/2023); Maharashtra Civil Engineering Services Main Examination, 2025 (003/2026); and Maharashtra Electrical Engineering Services Main Examination, 2025 (012/2026).
Article Summary: All hearings of the Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) inquiry commission will be open to the public at the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) headquarters in BKC, Bandra East. FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe said the panel’s office has been established on the second floor, room 201, within the FDA building.

Article Title: HC seeks details of 14 Mumbai schools facing closure
Article Text:
The PIL in Bombay High Court challenged action taken by BMC’s education department

Mumbai:





Bombay High Court has directed BMC to give details of 14 English primary schools running classes one to four in Malwani, Malad (W) against which it has initiated action for closure.Chief Justice M C Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna on Wednesday said they would examine “under what circumstances the concerned/competent authorities have permitted the said schools to perpetuate such a situation.” “At the same time, we are also conscious of the future of the students who are receiving education in such schools/institutions,” they added.The PIL by Nazir Khan, a private tutor, challenged action taken by BMC’s education department to close the 14 schools due to non-recognition under the Right to Education Act, without providing an alternate remedy or ensuring effective continuity of education to the students, in violation of Article 21A (Right to Education).His petition said no proper hearing was given before an FIR was registered on June 18. Khan urged the high court to quash and set aside BMC’s closure notices, direct Malwani police station not to take any coercive action against the schools and direct that all schools be permitted to continue so that students’ academic year is not wasted.He also sought, pending hearing, a stay on the notices and on further administrative or criminal proceedings.BMC’s advocate Poornima Kantharia said several notices were issued to the schools not to begin fresh admissions. Despite this, they are inducting students and even imparting education.The judges noted the petition listed the names of 14 schools against which an FIR is registered. The schools are Little World, Father Abraham, Little Wonders, Rose Mary, Jhil, Daya Sagar, Cosmos, Sadhana, ISM, MH, Crescent, Indian Glory, Happy Valley and Archivas Learning Campus.Before proceeding on merits, the judges directed BMC’s competent authority to file an affidavit regarding status of authorisation of the schools, whether they are aided, non-aided or otherwise, the number of students and teachers, whether the schools are affiliated to any recognised board, their date of operation and action, if any, taken against the schools and/or their management.“Considering the plight of the students receiving education in such schools/institutions,” the judges may also examine “if some relaxation may be accorded to enable such students to complete their current academic year.”“Our concern and anxiety is that the current academic year of such students should not be disturbed and/or unsettled mid-stream, which would cause grave and irreparable prejudice to them,” the judges said. They posted the next hearing on Nov 4.
Article Summary: Bombay High Court has directed BMC to give details of 14 English primary schools running classes one to four in Malwani, Malad (W) against which it has initiated action for closure. PIL by Nazir Khan, a private tutor, challenged action taken by BMC’s education department to close the 14 schools due to non-recognition.

Article Title: 1 more arrest in Tiger Shroff firing case; 11 in police custody till Nov 6
Article Text:
Mumbai:





The city crime branch police have arrested one more person from Haryana in the Tiger Shroff firing case. The accused, Aman , a resident of Rohna village in Haryana, was apprehended by a team of the crime branch unit in Kharkhoda after it received information about money being credited to his bank account. Aman is the 12th accused to be arrested in the case.During the investigation, police found that Kunal Sunjay, another accused from Rohna, had deposited money into Aman’s account. Transactions of Rs 5,000 each from several other accounts were also detected. He will be produced in the special court Friday.Meanwhile on Thursday, the special court, noting that a “deep-rooted conspiracy” required detailed custodial interrogation, remanded the other 11 accused to police custody till Nov 6, accepting the Crime Branch’s submission that the alleged organized crime syndicate’s financial network, digital trail and weapons supply chain had to be probed. This was the first remand hearing of the accused after the invocation of Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA).Seeking 10 days’ custody, the prosecution submitted the accused were “digitally equipped” and had used hidden foreign applications like Signal and Zangi, as well as Aadhaar cards, to conceal their identity and hide communications relating to the alleged organized crime activity. Consequently, the provisions of the Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016 were also invoked.Special judge Satyanarayan R Navandar pronounced the order after the city Crime Branch produced the accused, including two women, before the court for remand. Appearing for the prosecution, special public prosecutor Sunil Gonsalves told the court that MCOCA had been invoked after the role of alleged gang leader and absconding accused Anil Pandit emerged. Gonsalves submitted that Pandit had formed an organized crime syndicate to regain or establish supremacy in Mumbai and had recruited multiple accused from across Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. The prosecution said the case involved two coordinated modules. Fulsingh Kumar, Rehan Ansari, Ritik Mahato, Ankit Khatak and Sameer Khatri allegedly conducted recce and participated in the actual firing, while Radha Verma, Babita Rao, Kunal Jaminsingh, Sumit Saroliya, Jatin Panchal and Pranjal Thakran allegedly formed the weapons-delivery team.“The possible involvement of more accused and the larger ramifications of the alleged conspiracy also require investigation. These aspects are material to ascertain the respective roles of the accused and their alleged connections with the absconding accused and other members of the syndicate... the requirement of further custodial interrogation cannot be said to be unjustified merely because certain articles have already been seized and digital material has been retrieved,” the judge noted.
Article Summary: Aman, a resident of Rohna village in Haryana, was apprehended by a team of the crime branch unit in Kharkhoda. Aman is the 12th accused to be arrested in the case. The other 11 accused were remanded to police custody till Nov 6.

Article Title: 3 rescued, one feared trapped as under-construction building slab collapses in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar
Article Text:
Search operation underway at the site of the collapsed building in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Three workers were rescued after the roof slab of an under-construction commercial building collapsed on Jalna Road in the Chikalthana area of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. One more worker is feared trapped under the rubble, with rescue teams continuing their search operation.The incident occurred while concrete was being poured for the first-floor roof. Preliminary information suggests that the iron pipes supporting the structure bent under the load, causing the slab to collapse.Around 15 workers were at the site when the incident occurred. While several managed to escape, some were caught beneath the debris. Three workers were rescued, two of whom sustained injuries and were taken to hospital.Senior Police Inspector of CIDCO MIDC, G S Raire, said, “15 workers were working at the construction site when the slab collapsed. While eight to nine workers managed to escape, four were present at the lower level. Of these, two sustained injuries and were shifted to a hospital, one managed to come out safely, while one worker remains trapped under the debris.”"The rescue operation has been underway since yesterday, and we are making every possible effort to bring the trapped worker out safely. Our senior officers, including the ACP, DCP and Commissioner of Police, have visited the site and are guiding the operation. We have also deployed a canine unit to assist in the search," Raire said.The fire brigade, police and rescue personnel rushed to the location and began clearing the rubble using heavy equipment, including JCB machines, cranes and two Poclain excavators. A canine unit was also pressed into service to help locate the missing worker.Raire said municipal corporation officials, medical personnel and police teams were at the site to assist with the operation. However, the hardened and tightly packed debris has made the rescue effort difficult."We have deployed machines, but the rescue operation is challenging because the debris has become very compacted. Our teams are working continuously, and we are making every effort to complete the rescue as quickly as possible. We are confident that we will succeed," he said.Senior police officials, including the ACP, DCP and Commissioner of Police, visited the site to review the situation and supervise the rescue efforts. The operation was continuing as teams worked to reach the trapped worker.
Article Summary: The incident occurred while concrete was being poured for the first-floor roof. Around 15 workers were at the site when the incident occurred. Three workers were rescued, two of whom sustained injuries and were taken to hospital. One more worker is feared trapped under the rubble, with rescue teams continuing their search.

Article Title: Latur police team attacked during midnight raid in Hingoli; assistant inspector among 6 cops injured
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





An assistant inspector suffered serious head injuries and five other policemen were hurt after a group of people allegedly attacked a Latur crime branch team with sticks and iron rods, hurled chilli powder into their eyes and damaged a police vehicle during a midnight raid in Palshi village of Hingoli district.The attack took place around 12.20am on Thursday when the local crime branch team from Latur reached the village to arrest burglary accused Raju Mohan Shinde.According to the FIR, the team led by assistant inspector Pandurang Mane was confronted by a group of men and women who allegedly formed an unlawful assembly and attacked the police personnel to prevent the arrest. Mane sustained a serious head injury after being struck with a rod. Sub-inspector Amar Kendre was also hit on the head, while four other personnel suffered other injuries in the assault.The attackers allegedly threw chilli powder into the policemen’s eyes, hampering their response and allowing the accused to resist arrest. The mob then allegedly pelted stones at the police vehicle and smashed its windowpanes, causing damage estimated at Rs 10,000.All injured police personnel were taken to the Hatta primary health centre for treatment before returning to Latur.Following the attack, Hingoli police registered a case under multiple sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, including attempt to murder, assault on public servants, unlawful assembly and rioting.The four accused named in the FIR are Vicky Shinde (32), Sudarshan Shinde (37), Sachin Shinde (34) and Raju Shinde (32), all residents of Palshi village. Three to four other unidentified men and women have also been booked.The incident prompted a swift police response. Additional SP Kamlesh Meena reviewed the situation and dispatched multiple teams to track down the accused. Three Hingoli police teams have been pressed into service to apprehend those involved in the attack.Police said the assault not only left six personnel injured but also obstructed officers from carrying out a lawful arrest operation. The investigation is being conducted by sub-inspector Amar Kendre.
Article Summary: An assistant inspector suffered serious head injuries and five other policemen were hurt after a group of people allegedly attacked a Latur crime branch team with sticks and iron rods. The attack took place during a midnight raid in Palshi village of Hingoli district. The attackers allegedly threw chilli powder into the policemen’s eyes, hampering their response and allowing the accused to resist arrest.

Article Title: Nine held in Nanded farmer death case; SIT arrests finance firm operators
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





The Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the death of farmer Chandrakant Shinde has arrested nine people so far, including the alleged prime accused, finance operators, a partner and a manager linked to a microfinance firm.Shinde’s body was found at the office of KF Enterprises near Hingoli Gate bridge in Nanded city last week. Police have registered a case of murder and kidnapping against the finance firm and its associates.In the latest operation, the SIT, Vazirabad police and local crime branch personnel arrested three more accused from Nanded and Parbhani. They were identified as Harpreet Singh, alias Gandu (40), a finance operator from Abchalnagar in Nanded; Satpal Singh Khalsa (47), a finance operator and secretary of Kuberfal Credit Society; and Sheikh Shoeb Sheikh Mehmud (21), an employee allegedly associated with Khalsa Finance.With these arrests, the total number of accused held in the case has risen to nine.Earlier, police had arrested Jaykumar alias Shera Bhagwan Gaikwad (22), Sheikh Amer Sheikh Saheb Hussain (25), Ian Khan (40) and Sheikh Mudassir Sheikh Khadir (24) on Oct 26. KF Finance partner Sheikh Ahmed alias Aslam Mohammed Bashir (38) and manager Sumedh Shekojirao Doibale (21) were arrested a day later.The first four accused have been remanded in police custody till Thursday, while Ahmed and Doibale have been sent to police custody till Oct 31.The case was registered at Vazirabad police station on Oct 24 after Shinde’s wife lodged a complaint. Police invoked charges under sections 103(1), 140(1), 140(2), 142, 127(2) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.“Considering the seriousness of the incident, we have constituted an SIT to ensure a thorough and impartial investigation. Farmers and residents facing illegal harassment, threats or coercion by finance companies should not take any extreme step out of fear or emotional distress. They should immediately approach the nearest police station or call the emergency helpline 112. Strict legal action will be taken against those found responsible,” said Nanded superintendent of police Neelabh Rohan.Police said the investigation is focused on the role of those associated with the finance operations and the circumstances that led to Shinde’s death.
Article Summary: Chandrakant Shinde’s body was found at the office of KF Enterprises near Hingoli Gate bridge in Nanded city last week. Police have registered a case of murder and kidnapping against the finance firm and its associates. In the latest operation, the SIT, Vazirabad police and local crime branch personnel arrested three more accused.

Article Title: Latur farmer suicide: Case against micro finance firm staff over alleged loan recovery harassment
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





Police have registered a case against officials and employees of four financial institutions for allegedly abetting the suicide of a 26-year-old farmer from Latur district, bringing fresh scrutiny on aggressive loan recovery practices and harassment linked to microfinance and digital lending.Dattatraya Kumbhar, a resident of Rani Ankulega village in Shirur Anantpal taluka, died by suicide at his home on Oct 26. Based on a complaint filed by his wife, Savita Kumbhar, Shirur Anantpal police registered a case under section 108 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).The FIR alleges that Kumbhar was subjected to repeated calls and mental harassment over loan repayments. Family members told police that the recovery calls continued even after his death, with callers allegedly demanding money despite being informed that he had died.Latur additional superintendent of police Mangesh Chavan said police were identifying the employees who contacted Kumbhar before and after his death and examining the role of officials linked to the four financial institutions.Police said the probe will focus on the nature of the alleged recovery pressure, the frequency of the calls and the responsibility of those involved.The case has also renewed concerns over the treatment of borrowers who avail small loans through digital lending platforms and later struggle to meet repayment demands.Kumbhar is survived by his elderly mother, wife and two young children. The family was already reeling under drought, crop losses and mounting debt when the alleged harassment occurred.Latur superintendent of police Amol Tambe said vulnerable borrowers often become easy targets. “Gullible people in desperate need of loans end up falling prey to the traps of private moneylenders, micro finance companies including the online applications that charge hefty interest rates. We have been told that the recovery agents go to unbelievable extents, even when there is a single delay in paying the instalments. We have appealed citizens to come forward and lodge a complaint against any such harassment by private moneylenders and such micro finance companies and applications,” Tambe said.An officer from the Economic Offences Wing said investigators were hearing similar complaints from borrowers caught in loan recovery disputes. “The experiences being narrated by the victims of such loan traps have raised concerns about transparency in digital lending, the accuracy of loan closure records and the methods used by recovery agents,” the officer said.Police said the investigation is continuing and action will be taken against those found responsible for the alleged harassment.
Article Summary: Dattatraya Kumbhar, a 26-year-old farmer from Latur district, died by suicide at his home on Oct 26. Police have registered a case against officials and employees of four financial institutions for allegedly abetting the suicide. Family members told police that the recovery calls continued even after his death.

Article Title: Jalna admin initiates adopt drought-hit villages drive
Article Text:
The campaign aims to ensure that every family in drought-hit villages remains safe, has access to water and receives support until the rains return

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





As drought tightens its grip on Jalna district, collector Ashima Mittal has launched the ‘Gaon Dattak’ initiative, urging NGOs, corporates, industrial houses, elected representatives and citizens to adopt villages and support them until the next monsoon.Responding to the appeal, Jalna district guardian minister Pankaja Munde has announced that she will adopt Antarwali Sarati, the epicentre of the Maratha reservation movement led by Manoj Jarange.Mittal said people can contribute by lending to farmers and women’s self-help groups through Rang De, an RBI-regulated peer-to-peer lending platform. They can also support a rural family, buy goods from village producers, visit villages and participate in family and community occasions, including births, mass weddings and festivals.“Funds will be accepted only through recognised CSR and donation channels, and only for verified needs. PDS, MGNREGA and govt tankers will continue under the district plan,” Mittal said.Running for nine months, from Oct 2026 to June 2027, the campaign aims to ensure that every family in drought-hit villages remains safe, has access to water and receives support until the rains return.As per the available data, Jalna received 452.7 mm rain this monsoon against the average of 616.2 mm, a deficit of 26%.All eight talukas have triggered the first stage of the drought code.Ghansawangi recorded 38.7% below-average rainfall, followed by Ambad (35.4%) and Partur (29.9%). Groundwater has dropped by an average 3.69 metres, and 47 out of the 67 irrigation projects are dry or in dead storage. Fodder for 6.33 lakh animals will last here only 62 days.Officials estimate 937 villages and wadis will face water scarcity by June 2027, 502 of them by Dec. Tanker deployment, at 29 now, is planned to go up to 135 at peak demand.“The administration is handling tankers, wages and fodder, but it cannot reach every household alone. Gaon Dattak links each village with a committed supporter and a helpline,” Mittal said.About 250 priority villages among 971 will be allotted to partners in the first phase. Each taluka will have a helpline staffed by a trained team member, allowing callers to choose “I need help” or “I want to help”.An eight-member district crisis team, with one member from each taluka, will prioritise cases and follow up until resolution. Each village will nominate two or three contact persons, including a talathi, gram sevak, teacher or ASHA worker, to ensure delivery.Mittal will review progress monthly, with milestones on Nov 26 and Jan 10. Those wishing to participate can call their taluka helpline: 7378910442, 7378910458, 7378910465, 7378910478, 7378910482, 7378910483, 7378910487 or 7378910496.
Article Summary: The campaign aims to ensure that every family in drought-hit villages remains safe, has access to water and receives support until the rains return. Jalna received 452.7 mm rain this monsoon against the average of 616.2 mm, a deficit of 26%. All eight talukas have triggered the first stage of the drought code.

Article Title: Reel star Sabale springs surprise, takes third spot in Aurangabad Graduate poll
Article Text:
Raviraj Sabale

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Reel star and independent candidate Raviraj Sabale emerged as a surprise performer in the Aurangabad Graduate constituency election, securing more than 19,000 first-preference votes and finishing third, according to the latest counting trends.Sabale outpolled Shiv Sena (UBT) candidate Dilip Ghuge, who secured over 8,000 votes. Known for his Marathi reels on jobs, education and Marathwada politics, Saable was contesting his maiden election.Reacting to the trends, Sabale thanked graduate voters and said his campaign was aimed at amplifying the concerns of graduates. “This is just the beginning. I entered the race to raise the voice of graduates who feel unheard. The love I got from voters shows that content can become a campaign,” he said.Without naming any rival, Sabale claimed he had “swallowed” an established politician and ended an 18-year “drought”, an apparent reference to former MLC Satish Chavan, who had won three consecutive terms.Political observers, however, said Sabale’s candidature may have hurt NCP (SP) candidate Pratapsinh Patil more than Chavan. A vocal supporter of quota activist Manoj Jarange, Sabale had frequently targeted chief minister Devendra Fadnavis and the state govt through his social media content. Observers believe a significant portion of the votes polled by Sabale may otherwise have gone to Patil.
Article Summary: Independent candidate Raviraj Sabale emerged as a surprise performer in the Aurangabad Graduate constituency election. He secured more than 19,000 first- preference votes and finished third. Sabale outpolled Shiv Sena (UBT) candidate Dilip Ghuge, who secured over 8,000 votes.

Article Title: 10kg ganja worth Rs 6 lakh seized, 2 women arrested
Article Text:
Anti-narcotics cell seizes 10kg ganja worth Rs 6.19 lakh, two women held

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





The anti-narcotics cell of the city police seized over 10kg of ganja, a mobile phone and a two-wheeler collectively worth Rs 6.2 lakh, and arrested two women near Waluj for allegedly possessing the contraband for sale.The accused were identified as Sunita Pimple (32) and Komal Pawar (22), both residents of the Khandoba temple area in Satara village.Police said the action was taken on Tuesday after the anti-narcotics cell (ANC) received specific information about ganja being transported for sale. A team intercepted the women near Hotel Yograj on the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar-Ahilyanagar road and recovered the suspected contraband.Assistant inspector Sachin Jadhav said police seized the ganja and other articles and were probing the source of the supply as well as the involvement of other suspects.Preliminary investigation indicated that the women had allegedly procured the contraband from Mahesh Gaikwad of Gadhe Pimpalgaon in Vaijapur taluka. Police said his role was under investigation.A case under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act has been registered at Waluj police station against the two women and others.Commissioner of police Pravin Pawar said the city police were continuing their crackdown on the sale and distribution of narcotic substances. He appealed to citizens to share credible information about drug peddling and substance abuse so that police could take timely action.Police have urged citizens to report instances of drug sales, consumption and the use of premises for substance abuse. Information can be shared with the anti-narcotics cell through WhatsApp on 9684702002.
Article Summary: Anti-narcotics cell of the city police seized over 10kg of ganja, a mobile phone and a two-wheeler collectively worth Rs 6.2 lakh. The accused were identified as Sunita Pimple (32) and Komal Pawar (22)

Article Title: Cyber attack cripples services at Kamalnayan Bajaj Hospital; billing, insurance claims hit
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





A ransomware attack on the servers of Kamalnayan Bajaj Hospital has severely disrupted patient services, paralysing billing operations, health insurance processing and treatment benefits under govt schemes since Oct 18. With the Hospital Management Information System (HMIS) rendered inaccessible, patients have reportedly been facing delays in treatment, medicine dispensing and claim settlements.Police have registered an FIR against unidentified cyber criminals after the hospital alleged that all nine of its servers were hacked, data was encrypted and a ransom was demanded for its release. The attack has affected one of the leading hospitals in the Marathwada region and brought much of its digital operations to a standstill.According to the complaint, the breach came to light around 3 am on Oct 18 when billing staff found that bills could not be generated as the HMIS had stopped functioning. Prashant Pandey, the hospital’s IT department head, was alerted and he found the server inaccessible, displaying an “access denied” message. The firewall could not be accessed and antivirus logs reportedly indicated a virus attack across all nine servers.Pandey declined to comment on the investigation.Police said a ransom note later appeared on the system. The note, purportedly from a group calling itself “Crypto24 Group”, claimed hospital files had been encrypted and sensitive data stolen. It warned that the data would be published on a Tor-based leak site unless contact was established within a stipulated period.The FIR states that patient care, billing, insurance processing, reporting and several other hospital functions were affected after the attack. Services related to medicines and billing under the HMIS were also hit, causing inconvenience to patients.“The services have not stopped, they have just slowed down,” said hospital executive committee member Dr Milind Vaishnav. “We have informed all the authorities concerned, including those heading govt schemes, about the situation. We have a disaster management plan in place and it has been executed,” Vaishnav added.Based on Pandey’s complaint, Satara area police registered a case under section 308 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and relevant provisions of the Information Technology Act. Inspector Krushnachandra Shinde is investigating the case.Shinde said the hospital first reported the incident to CERT-In, the national cyber security agency, and provided the required technical information before approaching the police.Hospital sources claimed the attack had caused substantial financial losses and severely hampered day-to-day operations. However, police said the complaint does not disclose the amount of ransom allegedly demanded by the hackers.
Article Summary: Kamalnayan Bajaj Hospital in Marathwada was hit by a ransomware attack on Oct 18. Patients have reportedly been facing delays in treatment, medicine dispensing and claim settlements. Police have registered an FIR against unidentified cyber criminals after the hospital alleged that all nine of its servers were hacked.
